item.title: UK Sanctions 12 More ‘Shadow-Fleet’ Tankers as Russia’s Arctic Traffic Grows
item.dc:creator: Malte Humpert
item.description: The United Kingdom on Thursday sanctioned 12 oil tankers it identified as part of Russia's shadow fleet, including the 22-year-old Dakar that is currently making an unusual late-season voyage on the Northern Sea Route.

item.title: Turkey Says Russia, Ukraine Increasing Attacks in Black Sea Ahead of Winter
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: Intensifying attacks by Russia and Ukraine ahead of the winter are further endangering navigational safety in the Black Sea, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Thursday, adding that world powers must not allow the region to be turned into a new front in the war.

item.title: Subcontinent Ports Benefiting from Geopolitical Disruptions
item.dc:creator: Lori Ann LaRocco
item.description: Today's trade flows resemble a windy waterpark slide more than the traditional waterway superhighway. The three-dimensional chess game being played by ocean carriers and tankers has delivered big bucks in day rates, container rates, and surcharges. But there is a group of winners not currently being highlighted.

item.title: Mexican Auto Exports Slump in September as US Tariffs Take Toll
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: Mexico's auto exports posted their biggest slump so far this year, data from statistics office INEGI showed on Wednesday, a decline analysts attributed to tariff policies from the US, the biggest market for the Latin American country's top industrial sector.

item.title: India Shuns Costly Russian Oil as Middle East Flows Recover
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.description: Indian refiners have cut back Russian crude purchases for November delivery, as rising competition from China pushes up prices at a time when buyers can tap alternative shipments from the Middle East.

item.title: Sanctioned 22-Year-Old Tanker Makes Rare Late-Season Arctic Voyage
item.dc:creator: Malte Humpert
item.description: A 22-year-old product tanker sanctioned by the European Union is making an unusual late-season voyage along Russia's Northern Sea Route, highlighting the growing use of older, lower-specification vessels to move petroleum products through the Arctic.

item.title: South Korea Denies Ukrainian Report That It Eased Russia’s Fuel Crisis
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: South Korea's presidential office on Wednesday dismissed a Ukrainian report that Russia has imported petroleum products from South Korean ports, calling the accusation inappropriate.

item.title: Port of Savannah Sets September Container Record as Imports Rise
item.dc:creator: Mike Schuler
item.description: The Port of Savannah handled a record 504,015 twenty-foot equivalent units in September, up 3.7% from a year earlier as strong imports and a later-than-usual peak season boosted volumes.

item.title: Trafigura Buys Seven Oil Tankers From SFL as Shipping Costs Rise
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.description: Trafigura Group bought seven oil tankers from New York-listed SFL Corp., in the latest example of how trading houses and state energy companies are acquiring vessels to ship crude and products.
